White’s 1. b3 is a quiet, preparatory move: it intends Bb2 and puts the bishop on the long diagonal, but it creates no immediate tactical threat. Black should take the center while developing naturally. Playing 1...e5 grabs central space and opens good lines for Black’s pieces. If White continues 2.Bb2, Black can answer 2...Nc6, defending the e5-pawn while developing; White cannot grab the pawn cheaply. Black can follow up with Nf6, d6, Bc5/Be7, and castling.

Move: e5
